newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan sees inflation premium of over 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sees inflation premium of over 3.0 pct.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan Tuesday, noting that the current inflation premium is more that 3.0 percent, said that rates would take a dramatic drop as a result of a balanced budget.
"We still have embodied in long-term interest rates inflation expectations which possibly exceed three percent," he said.

He added that "if we can eliminate the long-term inflation that is embodied in the budget beyond the year 2002 we can find ourselves with fairly dramatic, further declines in long term rates from current levels in the not-too-distant future."

He said that this was provided "we set into law a credible change in budget practices that addresses not only the year 2002 but the problems that are likely to emerge under current law subsequent to that."
Greenspan also voiced scepticism about the practical usefulness of the so-called NAIRU concept for monetary policy.

That concept posits that there is a non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment for the economy as whole. If the jobless rate is below that, inflation tends to increase. If it is above that, inflation tends to subside.
"It's a very useful statistic for a model," Greenspan said. "But it is so unstable when you try to apply it to the real world that I am very dubious about its practical applicability."
